title: Teaching prayer
hookLine: a granddaughter on his shoulder, all the way through the prayer

cards: A man stands in prayer with a little girl up on his shoulder. When he goes down to prostrate, he sets her gently on the floor. When he stands again, he lifts her back up.
Sahih al-Bukhari tells it, in paraphrase: the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, prayed while carrying his granddaughter Umamah, the daughter of his daughter Zaynab. No lecture about prayer.
Just a child, riding along through it, watching every movement from up close.

teach.h: PRAY AT SEVEN: YEARS TO GROW INTO IT.
teach.b: Start with the instruction people quote. In Sunan Abu Dawud, in paraphrase, the Prophet said: command your children to pray when they are seven years old.

The same hadith goes on to speak of the age of ten with firmer words, and scholars discuss what that firmness should and shouldn't mean. But notice the order. Seven comes first, three years before the firmer words.
A child isn't asked to pray as an adult does; they're given time to grow into it. Second, the Qur'an puts this in a parent's mouth.

teach.h: O MY DEAR SON! ESTABLISH WORSHIP.
teach.b: In surah Luqman, a wise father advises his son, and when he comes to prayer, in Pickthall's translation, he says: "O my dear son! Establish worship." The words are tender before they're firm.
Third, the Prophet didn't treat a child as an interruption.

Umamah on his shoulder, down when he prostrates, up when he stands: every movement of the prayer, seen from the closest seat in the room. Arabic has a word for what he was being: a qudwah, an example to follow.
A child copies the bow before understanding it, and learns the words from hearing them said nearby. Fourth, the line that ties it together.
The Qur'an tells the Prophet, in Pickthall's words: "And enjoin upon thy people worship, and be constant therein." Tell others, and keep doing it yourself.
The instruction and the example travel together, and without the example, the instruction has nothing to point to.

how: Muslim parents who follow the hadith in Abu Dawud begin teaching children the prayer around the age of seven, and children often learn it by praying beside their parents at home and in the mosque.

p: the age to begin, in Abu Dawud

s: the hadith in Abu Dawud tells parents to start at seven

Luqman's advice about prayer is a bare command, with no tenderness in it

games.q: you're praying with your small granddaughter up on your shoulder. it's time to go down and prostrate. what do you do?
o: stop the prayer and hand her to someone.
set her down gently, and lift her again when you stand.
games.why: that's what Bukhari reports: down when he prostrated, up when he stood. the child stayed, and watched the whole prayer.

practice: If you pray and there's a child in your life, picture the next prayer you could let them watch, or join, or just sit beside, with no correcting.
If there's no child near you, remember the first person you watched do something devoted, pray, read, give, light a candle, and what the small one watching took away.
